newsitem.title: USA: Marathon, Ashland form oil refining venture.
newsitem.headline: Marathon, Ashland form oil refining venture.

text.p: USX Corp. said Thursday its USX-Marathon Group subsidiary has agreed to form a joint venture with Ashland Inc. combining the major elements of their refining, marketing and transportation operations.
The companies said job cuts and reassignments were likely, but did not specify how many workers would be affected.

Under terms of a letter of intent, USX-Marathon will own a 62 percent stake in the venture, which will include Ashland's refinery-produced petrochemicals. Ashland, based in Russell, Ky., will own 38 percent.

The venture, to be based in Findlay, Ohio, will not include the companies' exploration, production and chemical businesses. Other exclusions include Ashland's Valvoline division, along with equity investments in certain pipelines for both companies.

Current plans are to maintain the existing brands of each company. Marathon Oil Co., part of USX-Marathon, markets its products under the Marathon as well as other brands through its Emro Marketing Co. -- Speedway, Bonded, Cheker, Starvin' Marvin, United, Gastown, Wake Up and Kwik Sak. Ashland brands include Ashland, Super America and Rich Oil.
The new company may make future decisions on brand identification or consolidation, USX said.

"The goal of this joint venture is to create a competitive enterprise which capitalises on the strengths and complementary assets of both companies," said Thomas Usher, chairman of Pittsburgh-based USX.
"Market conditions have dictated that new approaches be explored to improve performance and growth opportunities."

The companies said they expect the joint venture to achieve substantial benefits largely by pursuing operational efficiencies and integrating their operations. This will not be achieved by closing major facilities, but future decisions will depend on business conditions, they added.

J. L. "Corky" Frank, Marathon's executive vice president of refining, marketing and transportation, will become president of the venture, which has yet to be named. Duane Gilliam, Ashland Petroleum's executive vice president, will become executive vice president.
The deal is subject to regulatory reviews, definitive agreements and approval by the boards of USX and Ashland.
Ashland's other businesses include coal and highway construction.
Ashland's stock rose 50 cents to $46, while Marathon rose 75 cents to $28.875 early on the New York Stock Exchange.
